newsitem.title: UK: UK hails WTO infotech pact as "tremendous news".
newsitem.headline: UK hails WTO infotech pact as "tremendous news".

text.p: Britain on Friday welcomed a World Trade Organisation (WTO) trade pact between 28 countries to eliminate tariffs on a range of high-technology products by the year 2000, saying it was "tremendous news" for the industry.

Trade Minister Ian Lang said the Information Technology Agreement, which may yield duty savings of around 250 million stg per year on both imports and exports, was an important breakthrough in the 305 billion stg hi-tech products industry.

"...it will reduce the cost of vital IT (information technology) products, such as semiconductors, and stimulate new growth and enterprise -- there is no British industry which does not rely on IT products in its operations," Lang said after a week-long inaugural ministerial conference in Singapore.

UK exporters would no longer have to pay duties in a number of key overseas markets, he noted. As well as the 15 European Union nations and the U.S., other countries including Japan, Canada, South Korea, Indonesia and Switzerland have said they may join the deal.

The WTO's Information Technology Agreement (ITA) will eliminate customs duties for participating countries by the turn of the century on a wide range of information technology products from computers to telephone handsets. Global trade in the IT sector is set to double to around 600 billion pounds by the year 2000, the UK Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said in a statement.
